A1.justification: Both complete 26-page PDFs describe the same work and contain matching main text and Appendices A–E. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the arXiv version stamp and Figure 4.

before.justification: v3 reports original 3DSSG experiments, including benchmark comparisons, encoder and component ablations, weakly supervised results, and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix D, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, weakly supervised evaluation, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Object-feature pretraining, the relationship encoder, LSE, GSE, BEG, and training losses remain identical. Figure 4 revises notation and styling without changing the components or connections described in Sections 3.1–3.4.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 3DSSG indoor-scene data derived from 3RScan and retain the same object, predicate, triplet, SGCls and PredCls tasks. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches in every corresponding comparison, including SGPN, SGFN, VL-SAT, Zhang et al., KERN in Table 10, and 3D-VLAP in Table 14. The loss variants in Table 6 are also unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, preprocessing, training budgets, model configurations, metrics, graph constraints and weak-supervision settings are identical, including the details in Appendices C–D.

E4.justification: The entropy–predicate-error analysis, encoder transfer tests, loss/modality/component/gating ablations, and embedding and scene-graph case studies are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the existing point estimates and entropy analysis are retained.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–14 and all empirical figures and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 2 retains object R@1 of 59.53, predicate R@1 of 91.27 and triplet R@50 of 91.40 for the proposed method.

T1.justification: Equations 1–20, the two formal assumptions, both propositions and their proofs are unchanged. Figure 4's notation corrections introduce no new mathematical definitions or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain identical claims about object-feature discrimination, encoder transferability, relationship modeling and performance under closed-vocabulary 3DSSG evaluation.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations, component-interaction interpretations and qualifications are identical. Appendices B and E retain the same idealized assumptions, open-vocabulary caveats, and limitations concerning object detection and incremental graph updates.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical software, hardware, hyperparameters, preprocessing, training times and checkpoint-selection details. The code availability statement and repository link are unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 64 references and related-work discussions are retained. Appendix A and the introduction make no changes to novelty claims or positioning relative to earlier research.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v3, dated 2 February 2026, to v5, dated 19 March 2026. The prose, headings, captions and main-text/appendix organization otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is reformatted with corrected geometric-descriptor notation, clearer embedding and loss labels, and restyled borders and typography. Its caption, placement and architectural connections remain unchanged; all other figures, tables and page layouts match.

improvement.justification: Figure 4 replaces a malformed geometric-input symbol with g_ij and more clearly typesets the refined embeddings and L1 loss, improving correspondence with the existing method and caption. This provides a limited improvement in explanatory clarity; the experimental evidence, theory and limitations are unchanged.
